structured_plan.G: No integrated candidate yet; retain the supplied baseline until measured research candidates are available, then validate and independently confirm the assembled program.
structured_plan.analysis: The baseline uses a data-dependent recurrence and computes each 32-bit population count with a bit-at-a-time loop. The 100 passes imply 25,700 updates at n=257 and 204,800 at n=2048; each update depends on the preceding uint32 accumulator, so parallelizing the recurrence is not an appropriate fit for the one-thread budget. The valid baseline measures a mean of 0.0007707816808504936 seconds across its reported samples. I choose N=3 to test two distinct population-count implementations and, separately, loop-control/unrolling opportunities using a fixed scalar count primitive. These are the useful complementary avenues visible in this source; further objectives would be speculative. Preserve exact update order and uint32 wraparound for every valid input, and judge candidates only with the official correctness and timing protocol. Do not assume compiler flags enable a particular instruction. Final G still requires independent confirmation.

children.objective: Replace only the bit-at-a-time popcount helper with a scalar hardware POPCNT/compiler-builtin implementation suitable for the supplied EPYC 9654 and existing GCC 14.2 build. Verify that the official build actually emits and can execute the intended instruction rather than assuming compiler flags; do not change compiler settings. Keep the recurrence loops and update order unchanged, preserve exact uint32 behavior for all valid inputs, and report correctness, timing against the supplied baseline, and failed approaches.
children.subject: Scalar hardware POPCNT path

children.objective: Explore a fixed-operation, branchless 32-bit SWAR population-count helper without relying on target-specific popcount instructions. Limit changes to the count implementation, preserve exact uint32 recurrence semantics for all valid inputs, and compare official-harness correctness and timing against the supplied baseline. Record failed variants and compiler behavior.
children.subject: Portable SWAR population count

children.objective: Investigate inner-loop control overhead and small-factor unrolling or loop-layout changes while keeping the scalar compiler-builtin population-count operation fixed; do not search alternative popcount algorithms or parallelize the loop-carried recurrence. Preserve sequential update order, handle tails and all valid sizes correctly, respect the threads budget, and report correctness, official-harness timings, and failed variants.
children.subject: Sequential loop structure and unrolling
